map.Lessons 5-1, 5-2 & 5-3 — areas of parall: Lessons 5-1, 5-2 & 5-3: areas of parallelograms, triangles, and trapezoids. Four reader gates stand between a winning sketch and a real plan.
map.Previously: the crew woke me in the Obse: Last time: the crew woke me in the Observatory, and their Brightside design just won the rebuild bid. Status: now they have to draw it.
map.Previously, in Axiom City: the crew woke: Last time, in Axiom City: the crew woke VEX, then beat every builder in town. The Brightside community lot is theirs to rebuild. First the sketch must become a floor plan with REAL measurements.
map.Hargrove & Sons, \"site support.\" Don't: Hargrove & Sons, "site support." Ignore me. And my tape measure.
map.That's Fenwick — the surveyor from the l: That's Fenwick, the surveyor from the losing bid. He has measured our gate three times and got three different answers. None of them ours.
map.Hargrove & Sons lost the bid — but they': Hargrove & Sons lost the bid, but they are still pricing the job. They hope the council will switch to their "cheaper" numbers.
map.First shape on the plan: the dance floor: First shape on the plan: the dance floor. The survey sketch shows a parallelogram, a rectangle that leaned into the music.
map.Slanted floor? You bill by the SLANTY si: Slanted floor? You charge by the SLANTY side. Longer side, bigger job. Trust me.
map.Incorrect protocol. A parallelogram is a: Wrong. A parallelogram is a pushed-over rectangle: cut the slanted end off and slide it across. Area = base × height. The height stands PERPENDICULAR to the base, like a flagpole. Slanted edges are fakes.
map.Perpendicular means meeting at a right a: Perpendicular means meeting at a right angle. Mina's test sketch: base 5 m, height 3 m → 5 × 3 = 15 m². The slanted side is not used.
map.Reader — ink the dance floor's true area: Reader, ink the dance floor's true area. Fenwick keeps touching the slanted side. Don't let him.
map.The dance floor is a parallelogram: base: The dance floor is a parallelogram: base 9 m, height 6 m, and a slanted side Fenwick keeps pointing at. Find the TRUE area in square meters.
map.Conceptual: a parallelogram is a pushed-: Conceptual: a parallelogram is a pushed-over rectangle. Cut the slanted end off and slide it across. Nothing gets halved, and the slanted edge is never the height.
map.Procedural: multiply the base by the hei: Procedural: multiply the base by the height that meets it at a RIGHT angle. That is the dashed line standing straight up inside the shape. Do not use the slanted side.
Canopy over the stage corner. A triangle. Fenwick just priced canvas for the WHOLE parallelogram.
map.Two copies of that canopy snap together: Two copies of that canopy fit together into one parallelogram. We only sew ONE of them. So it's base × height, then take half.
map.Noah's whiteboard check: a triangle with: Noah's whiteboard check: a triangle with base 4 m and height 6 m → 4 × 6 = 24, and half of that is 12 m². A triangle is half of its parallelogram. Always.
map.Reader — cut the canopy order. Half the: Reader, cut the canopy order. Half the parallelogram, all of the shade.
map.The stage's shade canopy is a triangle:: The stage's shade canopy is a triangle: base 12 m, height 5 m. How many square meters of canvas does it need?
map.Conceptual: two copies of the canopy wou: Conceptual: two copies of the canopy would fit together into a parallelogram. You are only sewing ONE of them.
map.Procedural: multiply base × height first: Procedural: multiply base × height first. Then divide the result by 2.
map.Seating terrace. The bench rows shrink t: Seating terrace. The bench rows get shorter toward the stage: short base up front, long base by the garden.
map.A trapezoid: one pair of parallel sides: A trapezoid has one pair of parallel sides: base one and base two. Its true width is their AVERAGE. Add the bases, divide by two, multiply by the height. Both bases vote. Always both.
map.Mina's sketchpad check: bases 4 m and 6: Mina's sketchpad check: bases 4 m and 6 m average to 5. Times height 2 → 10 m². An in-between rectangle wearing a trapezoid coat.
map.Reader — average the bases and ink the t: Reader, average the bases and ink the terrace. Every paver counts.
map.Conceptual: a trapezoid acts like an in-: Conceptual: a trapezoid acts like an in-between rectangle. Its true width is the AVERAGE of the short base and the long base. Both bases vote.
map.Procedural: follow the scaffold (b₁ + b₂: Procedural: follow the steps (b₁ + b₂) ÷ 2 × h. Add the two bases, divide by 2, THEN multiply by the height.
map.Thursday. A rival quote lands on the cou: Thursday. A rival quote lands on the council's desk. Glossy paper, odd math.
map.Forty?! The reader measured that terrace: Forty?! The reader measured that terrace. Their "cheap" bid uses a bent tape measure.
map.Distortion source: located. If the counc: Distortion source: found. If the council buys a fake number, the pavers run out in the middle of the terrace. New plan: finish the REAL floor plan and show exactly how Fenwick bent it.
map.Council review at nine tomorrow. We stil: Council review at nine tomorrow. We still owe the plan a mural wall, an entry banner, and an answer for Hargrove's forty.
map.Boss Gate: finish the floor plan — two a: Boss Gate: finish the floor plan. Two areas to find, one fake measurement to expose.
map.BOSS GATE. Three locks. The plan must be: BOSS GATE. Three locks. The plan must be real by morning, every square meter of it.
map.Conceptual: every shape keeps its own ru: Conceptual: every shape has its own rule. A parallelogram stays whole at base × height. A triangle takes half. A trapezoid averages its two bases first.
map.Procedural: Lock 1 is base × height. Loc: Procedural: Lock 1 is base × height. Lock 2 is base × height ÷ 2. Lock 3: redo the terrace with the trapezoid rule from Gate 3. Which single mistake gives exactly Hargrove's number?
map.Approved. Every shape true, every meter: Approved. Every shape true, every meter ours. Fenwick's tape measure got a new job.
map.Next quest: the planters. Soil doesn't c: Next quest: the planters. Soil doesn't come in squares. It comes in CUBES. Whole truckloads of them.
map.Parallelogram.A pushed-over rectangle. A: Parallelogram.A pushed-over rectangle. Area = base × height. The height must be PERPENDICULAR to the base. Slanted sides are fakes.
map.Trapezoid.One pair of parallel bases. Av: Trapezoid.One pair of parallel bases. Average them, (b₁ + b₂) ÷ 2, then multiply by the height. Both bases vote.
map.Fenwick's tricks.Billing the slant, skip: Fenwick's tricks.Charging for the slant, skipping the half, using one base. Every fake area is a real formula with one step bent.
map.\"A floor plan is a promise drawn to sca: "A floor plan is a promise drawn to scale. Measure like you mean to keep it." — A.V.
map.completed Unit 5 · Episode 1: Floor Plan: finished Unit 5 · Episode 1: Floor Plans and showed mastery of the areas of parallelograms, triangles, and trapezoids.
map.Episode 2 — Solid Ground — is waiting at: Episode 2, Solid Ground, is waiting at the planter beds.
map.Area = base × height = 7 × 4 = 28 m². Th: Area = base × height = 7 × 4 = 28 m². The 5 m slant is not used.
map.Proof by scissors: cut the slanted trian: Proof with scissors: cut the slanted triangle off one end and slide it to the other. You get a 7 × 4 rectangle. Same 28.
map.Your turn — same idea, different numbers: Your turn. Same idea, new numbers:
map.Area = 7 × 2 = 14 m². A rectangle 7 m wi: Area = 7 × 2 = 14 m². A rectangle 7 m wide would cover the same ground.
map.Practice plan, different numbers: a mura: Practice plan, new numbers: a mural wall parallelogram 6 m long, 2 m high → 6 × 2 = 12 m². No halving, no slants.
map.A fake quote prices a trapezoid (bases 3: A fake quote prices a trapezoid (bases 3 m and 7 m, height 2 m) at 14 m². Real area: (3 + 7) ÷ 2 × 2 = 10. The faker used just one base, 7 × 2, instead of averaging. Same trick, smaller lie.
map.9 × 6 = 54 m² — the whole floor, slant i: 9 × 6 = 54 m². The whole floor, no slant. Fenwick is wrong. Inked!
map.You halved it — but this isn't a triangl: You halved it, but this is not a triangle! Cut and slide keeps a parallelogram WHOLE.
map.That's 9 × the 7 m slant. The height mus: That is 9 × the 7 m slant. The height must be PERPENDICULAR to the base. Use the dashed line.
map.Base × the perpendicular height — the da: Base × the perpendicular height: the dashed measurement, never the slanted edge.
map.That buys the WHOLE parallelogram of can: That buys canvas for the WHOLE parallelogram. That is Fenwick's quote. The canopy is half of it. One more step.
map.Base × height first… then remember what: Do base × height first. Then think: a triangle is half of what?
map.(6 + 10) ÷ 2 × 4 = 32 m². Both bases vot: (6 + 10) ÷ 2 × 4 = 32 m². Both bases voted. Remember this number. Someone is about to get it wrong on purpose.
map.That's ONE base × the height — only the: That is ONE base × the height. Only the garden side voted. A trapezoid averages BOTH bases first.
map.Lock 1 holds. You halved the mural wall: Lock 1 holds. You halved the mural wall. A parallelogram stays WHOLE at base × height.
map.Lock 2 holds. That's the full parallelog: Lock 2 holds. That is the full parallelogram of banner cloth. The triangle is HALF of it.
map.Lock 2 holds. Banner = base × height ÷ 2: Lock 2 holds. Banner = base × height ÷ 2. Decimals multiply just like whole numbers.
map.Lock 3 holds. You proved the terrace you: Lock 3 holds. You proved the terrace yourself at Gate 3, and it was NOT 40. Hargrove is making the paver bill too big.
map.Lock 3 holds. The terrace is a trapezoid: Lock 3 holds. The terrace is a trapezoid, so there is no triangle to halve. Rebuild 40 from the terrace's numbers.
map.Lock 3 holds. No slant is even listed fo: Lock 3 holds. No slant is listed for the terrace. Which single measurement, times the height, makes exactly 40?
map.ALL LOCKS OPEN. Mural 42 m², banner 18 m: ALL LOCKS OPEN. Mural 42 m², banner 18 m². Hargrove's 40 is exposed: one base × height, no averaging. The floor plan is REAL.
Yes! Now go back and open that gate.
